title: Stop surfacing PinService's raw ArgumentError.message as OnboardingParentPinStep's error text
why: The domain layer's exception message is an English literal that reaches the presentation layer verbatim and unlocalized (PinService throws ArgumentError('PIN must be exactly 4 numeric digits') at pin_service.dart:65,135,199), so a Hebrew-locale parent sees this exact English sentence when setting up a child's PIN. It is also brittle cross-layer coupling: ArgumentError.message is typed Object?, so the `as String?` cast is only safe because every current throw site happens to pass a String -- changing any one of the three pin_service.dart throw sites to ArgumentError.value(...) would turn a benign validation failure into an unhandled TypeError in this catch block.
recommendation: Give PinService a typed error (enum or sealed class per EH-2/EH-6) instead of ArgumentError(String), and resolve the display string in the widget via AppLocalizations.
acceptance_criteria: PinService validation failure exposed as a typed value/enum, not ArgumentError with a formatted message
a test asserts the PIN-mismatch/invalid-PIN error text is resolved via AppLocalizations for both en and he locales

corrections: Failure scenario is guarded by core/widgets/pin_entry_widget.dart's per-digit digitsOnly/maxLength(1) formatters — pin.length!=4/!_isNumeric can't actually occur through this UI path, so the concrete i18n-cost claim is overstated; the architectural coupling/cast-fragility point still stands as P3 hygiene.
